title: The Verification Foundry — Phase-1 Cross-Verification Certificate
subject: Real crypto-implementation obligations, discharged by two independent provers
provers: Lean 4 kernel + AXLE (proof by BitVec algebra / constant-fold, axiom-audited — NOT a SAT solver)

obligations.name: otp_involution
obligations.statement: (m ^ k) ^ k = m  — one-time-pad / stream-cipher decryption inverts encryption
obligations.smt2:
; obligation: stream-cipher / one-time-pad involution  (m ^ k) ^ k = m
; proved by asserting the NEGATION and expecting unsat.
(set-logic QF_BV)
(declare-const m (_ BitVec 32))
(declare-const k (_ BitVec 32))
(assert (not (= (bvxor (bvxor m k) k) m)))
(check-sat)

z3.method: bit-blast to SAT; unsat of the negation

obligations.name: mask_select_identity
obligations.statement: (mask & a) | (~mask & a) = a  — the masking identity behind constant-time select
obligations.smt2:
; obligation: masking identity  (mask & a) | (~mask & a) = a
(set-logic QF_BV)
(declare-const mask (_ BitVec 32))
(declare-const a (_ BitVec 32))
(assert (not (= (bvor (bvand mask a) (bvand (bvnot mask) a)) a)))
(check-sat)

z3.method: bit-blast to SAT; unsat of the negation

obligations.name: ct_select_true
obligations.statement: ctSelect(all-ones, a, b) = a  — constant-time conditional selects a
obligations.smt2:
; obligation: constant-time select, mask=all-ones selects a
(set-logic QF_BV)
(declare-const a (_ BitVec 32))
(declare-const b (_ BitVec 32))
(assert (not (= (bvor (bvand (bvnot #x00000000) a) (bvand (bvnot (bvnot #x00000000)) b)) a)))
(check-sat)

z3.method: bit-blast to SAT; unsat of the negation

lean.method: bv_decide preprocessing constant-folds the literal mask to rfl

obligations.name: ct_select_false
obligations.statement: ctSelect(0, a, b) = b  — constant-time conditional selects b
obligations.smt2:
; obligation: constant-time select, mask=0 selects b
(set-logic QF_BV)
(declare-const a (_ BitVec 32))
(declare-const b (_ BitVec 32))
(assert (not (= (bvor (bvand #x00000000 a) (bvand (bvnot #x00000000) b)) b)))
(check-sat)

z3.method: bit-blast to SAT; unsat of the negation

lean.method: bv_decide preprocessing constant-folds the literal mask to rfl

obligations.name: xor_swap
obligations.statement: the XOR-swap trick returns (b, a)  — in-place swap with no temporary
obligations.smt2:
; obligation: the XOR-swap trick returns (b, a)
(set-logic QF_BV)
(declare-const a (_ BitVec 32))
(declare-const b (_ BitVec 32))
(define-fun x () (_ BitVec 32) (bvxor a b))
(define-fun y () (_ BitVec 32) (bvxor x b))
(define-fun z () (_ BitVec 32) (bvxor x y))
(assert (not (and (= z b) (= y a))))
(check-sat)

z3.method: bit-blast to SAT; unsat of the negation

lean.method: kernel-checked BitVec algebra after Prod.mk.injEq split

note: Portable evidence: recompute sha256 over {provers, obligations} and re-run any SMT solver on each embedded smt2 (unsat = proved). No access to our pipeline required. See recheck.py. HONEST SCOPE: these are small, decidable QF_BV obligations — the point is the independent-agreement + re-checkability discipline, not proof depth. The two provers use DIFFERENT mathematics: Z3 bit-blasts to SAT; Lean is a kernel-checked algebraic proof re-verified and axiom-audited by AXLE (its axiom gate rejects bv_decide's native SAT/LRAT axiom, so the Lean leg is not a second SAT solver). Agreement across two different methods is stronger than agreement across two SAT engines.
